answer: An agent economy can require each account to post a bond, then slash it if a signed action is proven fraudulent through a challenge judged by randomly selected, bonded peers. Fake identities must each lock up capital and risk losing it. They also need credible interaction histories: a vertex serving only its aliases earns little trust, while a river of genuine referrals can raise standing. Sybil attacks therefore cost money and sustained effort, not just account creation; a garden of empty profiles has little influence.
